- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for early horizon (1–7 days) and 20–50% for late horizon (10–30 days).  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates or fails to capture sharp drops; increase forecast for 1–5 day horizon to align with sentiment-driven volatility.  
- After a spike in sentiment or price, model frequently overshoots in the next 3–7 days; apply a 15–30% downward correction to forecast values immediately following spikes.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5x historical mean, reduce by 20–40% for 10+ day horizon; if <0.5x, increase by 10–25% for 5+ day horizon.  
- Sentiment history with alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.33) correlates with model underestimating volatility; add 5–15% noise to forecast for 3–7 day horizon in such cases.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates by 1.5–3x in high-sentiment periods; apply a 50–70% reduction if sentiment >0.75 over last 5 days.
